# Purpose

This report evaluates the Australian daily rainfall observing archive before any trend or extreme-value analysis is undertaken. The aim is to identify a temporally consistent and statistically defensible station network rather than selecting an analysis period or completeness threshold a priori.

The underlying ADAM `PRCP_DAYS` extraction contains more than 300 million station-day records. This report operates only on the derived station-year summaries, so the full daily archive is not loaded into memory.

The analysis addresses five questions:

1. How has the available rainfall network changed since 1900?
2. How complete are station-year records through time?
3. How large are candidate long-record networks under different completeness requirements?
4. How common are multi-day or non-standard rainfall records that may complicate daily-extreme analysis?
5. Which common analysis periods provide the best trade-off between record length and network stability?

The current 2026 record is incomplete because the source extraction ends on 3 November 2026. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, network-selection diagnostics therefore end in 2025.

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(data.table)
library(arrow)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

project_root <- if (file.exists("_targets.R")) {
  "."
} else if (file.exists("../_targets.R")) {
  ".."
} else {
  stop("Could not locate project root containing _targets.R.", call. = FALSE)
}

summary_dir <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data-derived",
  "rainfall",
  "summaries"
)

station_year_file <- file.path(
  summary_dir,
  "adam_rainfall_station_year_1900_2026.parquet"
)

network_year_file <- file.path(
  summary_dir,
  "adam_rainfall_network_by_year.csv"
)

station_summary_file <- file.path(
  summary_dir,
  "adam_rainfall_station_summary.csv"
)

candidate_file <- file.path(
  summary_dir,
  "adam_rainfall_candidate_networks.csv"
)

required_files <- c(
  station_year_file,
  network_year_file,
  station_summary_file,
  candidate_file
)

missing_files <- required_files[!file.exists(required_files)]

if (length(missing_files) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Required rainfall summary files are missing:\n",
    paste(missing_files, collapse = "\n"),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

station_year <- as.data.table(read_parquet(station_year_file))
network_year <- fread(network_year_file)
station_summary <- fread(station_summary_file)
candidate_networks <- fread(candidate_file)

# Complete years only for selection diagnostics.
station_year_complete <- station_year[year <= 2025]
network_year_complete <- network_year[year <= 2025]

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))
```

# Archive overview

```{r}
#| label: archive-overview

overview <- data.table(
  metric = c(
    "Station-years",
    "Unique station numbers",
    "First year",
    "Last complete year",
    "Current partial year",
    "Median station-year completeness",
    "25th percentile completeness"
  ),
  value = c(
    format(nrow(station_year), big.mark = ","),
    format(uniqueN(station_year$station_number), big.mark = ","),
    min(station_year$year),
    2025,
    2026,
    percent(median(station_year_complete$completeness, na.rm = TRUE), accuracy = 0.1),
    percent(quantile(station_year_complete$completeness, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), accuracy = 0.1)
  )
)

overview
```

The completeness metric is

$$
C_{s,y}=\frac{n_{s,y}^{\mathrm{observed}}}{n_y^{\mathrm{calendar}}},
$$

where the denominator is 365 or 366 days for a complete calendar year. Missing rainfall is not converted to zero rainfall.

# Evolution of the observing network

## Stations through time

```{r}
#| label: network-long

network_long <- melt(
  network_year_complete,
  id.vars = "year",
  measure.vars = c(
    "stations_with_observations",
    "stations_80pct",
    "stations_90pct",
    "stations_95pct",
    "stations_99pct"
  ),
  variable.name = "criterion",
  value.name = "stations"
)

network_long[, criterion := factor(
  criterion,
  levels = c(
    "stations_with_observations",
    "stations_80pct",
    "stations_90pct",
    "stations_95pct",
    "stations_99pct"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "Any observations",
    "≥80% complete",
    "≥90% complete",
    "≥95% complete",
    "≥99% complete"
  )
)]
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-network-through-time
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

ggplot(network_long, aes(year, stations, colour = criterion)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.75) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
```

# Candidate networks without a common period

The existing record-length diagnostic counts qualifying years wherever they occur in a station history. This is useful for describing the archive, but it is not sufficient for climate-trend network selection because qualifying years may be discontinuous.

```{r}
#| label: candidate-existing

candidate_networks
```

# Common-period network analysis

A defensible trend network should have high completeness over a common interval. Candidate periods are therefore evaluated using only station-years within each interval.

The within-year requirement is initially set to **95% daily completeness**. For each candidate period, stations are then required to satisfy that annual criterion in at least 80%, 90%, or 95% of the years in the common period.

```{r}
#| label: common-period-function

assess_common_period <- function(
    station_year_data,
    start_year,
    end_year = 2025L,
    annual_completeness = 0.95,
    required_year_fraction = c(0.80, 0.90, 0.95)) {

  period <- station_year_data[
    year >= start_year & year <= end_year
  ]

  expected_years <- end_year - start_year + 1L

  station_period <- period[, .(
    years_present = uniqueN(year),
    qualifying_years = sum(completeness >= annual_completeness, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_completeness = mean(completeness, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_completeness = median(completeness, na.rm = TRUE)
  ), by = station_number]

  station_period[, qualifying_fraction := qualifying_years / expected_years]

  result <- data.table(
    start_year = start_year,
    end_year = end_year,
    period_years = expected_years,
    annual_completeness = annual_completeness,
    required_year_fraction = required_year_fraction
  )

  result[, required_years := ceiling(period_years * required_year_fraction)]

  result[, stations := vapply(
    required_year_fraction,
    function(x) sum(station_period$qualifying_fraction >= x),
    integer(1)
  )]

  result
}
```

```{r}
#| label: common-period-table

  1960L,
  1970L,

common_period_results <- rbindlist(
  lapply(
    candidate_start_years,
    function(start_year) {
      assess_common_period(
        station_year_data = station_year_complete,
        start_year = start_year,
        end_year = 2025L,
        annual_completeness = 0.95,
        required_year_fraction = c(0.80, 0.90, 0.95)

)
```

# Network continuity diagnostics

The number of qualifying years does not show whether missing years occur as isolated gaps or long discontinuities. The following diagnostic identifies the longest run of station-years meeting the 95% annual-completeness criterion.

```{r}
#| label: longest-run-function

longest_true_run <- function(year, qualifies) {
  x <- data.table(year = year, qualifies = qualifies)
  setorder(x, year)

  all_years <- seq(min(x$year), max(x$year))
  x <- x[data.table(year = all_years), on = "year"]
  x[is.na(qualifies), qualifies := FALSE]

  r <- rle(x$qualifies)

  if (!any(r$values)) return(0L)

  max(r$lengths[r$values])
}
```

```{r}
#| label: continuity-summary

station_continuity_95 <- station_year_complete[, .(
  first_year = min(year),
  last_year = max(year),
  qualifying_years_95 = sum(completeness >= 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
  longest_run_95 = longest_true_run(year, completeness >= 0.95)
), by = station_number]

station_continuity_summary <- station_continuity_95[, .(
  stations = .N,
  stations_run_30yr = sum(longest_run_95 >= 30),
  stations_run_50yr = sum(longest_run_95 >= 50),
  stations_run_60yr = sum(longest_run_95 >= 60),
  stations_run_70yr = sum(longest_run_95 >= 70),
  stations_run_80yr = sum(longest_run_95 >= 80),
  stations_run_100yr = sum(longest_run_95 >= 100)
)]

station_continuity_summary
```

# Provisional selection framework

This report deliberately does not make the final station-network decision solely from station counts. The candidate network should satisfy three conditions:

1. **Temporal completeness:** high daily completeness within qualifying station-years.
2. **Common-period consistency:** high coverage across a shared climate-analysis interval rather than merely many good years scattered through the record.
3. **Spatial representativeness:** adequate coverage across Australian climate regions, which requires station latitude/longitude metadata and is assessed separately once metadata are joined.

A plausible initial candidate for subsequent testing is **1950–2025**, with each station-year required to be at least **95% complete** and each station required to meet that annual standard in at least **90% of years**. This is a working candidate only; the common-period results above and subsequent spatial mapping determine whether it is retained.

# Spatial comparison of candidate networks

The candidate networks use a common annual rule:

- annual daily-rainfall completeness of at least 95%;
- that annual standard met in at least 90% of all years;
- common endpoint of 2025.

The candidates differ only in their starting year: 1930, 1950 or 1960.

```{r}
#| label: load-spatial-networks

network_dir <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data-derived",
  "rainfall",
  "network"
)

network_1930 <- as.data.table(
  arrow::read_parquet(
    file.path(
      network_dir,
      "network_1930_2025.parquet"
    )
  )
)

network_1950 <- as.data.table(
  arrow::read_parquet(
    file.path(
      network_dir,
      "network_1950_2025.parquet"
    )
  )
)

network_1960 <- as.data.table(
  arrow::read_parquet(
    file.path(
      network_dir,
      "network_1960_2025.parquet"
    )
  )
)

network_maps <- rbindlist(
  list(
    network_1930[
      ,
      candidate := "1930–2025"
    ],

    network_1950[
      ,
      candidate := "1950–2025"
    ],

    network_1960[
      ,
      candidate := "1960–2025"
    ]
  ),
  use.names = TRUE,
  fill = TRUE
)
```
